#### About Dante Alighieri

Dante Alighieri (1265–1321) was the Florentine poet-philosopher of the Divine Comedy, exiled in the Guelf–Ghibelline conflicts. He wrote vernacular epic that synthesizes Aristotelian ethics, scholastic theology, and civic passion.

### Interpretation

Dante gives this to Francesca in the circle of the lustful, and it describes the specific structure of her punishment: she is not suffering a new loss but remembering a good she still knows as good. The pain comes from the contrast, which is why memory rather than fire is the instrument. In the Commedia this marks a departure from the usual economy of Hell, since the suffering depends on the person's own attachment remaining intact.

#### Why it matters

It identifies why some losses intensify rather than fade: what hurts is not the absence but the continued clarity of what was there.

### Questions readers arrive with

#### What is the source of the quotation “There is no greater pain than to recall…”?

“There is no greater pain than to recall…” comes from Inferno, V.121–123, attributed to Dante Alighieri.

#### What does Dante Alighieri mean by fate?

Across 4 recurring voices here (notably Epictetus and Seneca), fate is framed through Stoicism and Philosophy of Will. Some passages define fate; others warn how it fails; still others relocate it inside habit, community, or language. This passage enters that discussion through fate.
